items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: Jerry was a wonderful trumpet player... he just became a writer... Jerry would always, he would play everything he wrote before he brought it to a session... we were very busy running from one date to another date... Gary Grant was also involved with that sessions, in the trumpet section, the three

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and boy, I’m very happy to have Chuck Findley with me today. And one of your colleagues, who is a decent trumpet player named Jerry Hey said, “Chuck Findley can play anything.”

Well that’s a lovely compliment I must say, Monk. Well I’ll tell you that really goes back to like when we were recording the lovely Al Jarreau stuff and just a lot of ridiculous things. And Jerry was a wonderful trumpet player when he could play, but then he had an issue with his throat and he couldn’t play anymore so he just became a writer, which he was anyhow, and he became a fantastic commercial writer. But Jerry would always, he would play everything he wrote before he brought it to a session, and, to make…

That is so interesting because I went and revisited that and it’s literally four bars plus a two-beat pick-up. And the fact that it brought you that recognition and that — Herb Alpert had something to do with that song, didn’t he?

items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: Chuck Findley comes in at one minute to nine o’clock... And he played the living hell out of it. And at that point I was lucky to even play... we had to do it again, and Chuck played it better the next time.

ctx.x: Did you ever write something that you couldn’t play? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

If I couldn’t play it I wouldn’t write it. But yeah, back in the day it was anything goes back then. You know Chuck Findley can play anything. You know Gary’s amazing. And Bill Reichenbach on the trombone is also just a world class player. An amazing bass trombone player, trombone player, plays drums, great writer. And Larry Williams who also was in Seawind, and Dan Higgins who has been recently, who is just a brilliant musician. So you know you go in with those kind of guys like that, and now Wayne Bergeron…

Do you get ideas in your head even when you’re not really engaged in working? I guess I think I saw your dog come through the room. And when I take my dog for a walk if I’m working on an arrangement I get these things — you know I’m thinking more about how am I going to solve this little issue. I wonder if this happens to you?
